direct_ffi_candidates.netlink_add_tap: regular exported netlink tap registration function
direct_ffi_candidates.netlink_remove_tap: regular exported netlink tap unregistration function

linux/netdevice.h.reason: Expose `net_device`, `net_device_ops`, `dev_lstats_read`, flags, and per-cpu stat enums needed by nlmon planning.

linux/netlink.h.reason: Expose `netlink_tap`, tap registration functions, and `NLMSG_GOODSIZE` used by nlmon lifecycle/setup planning.

net/net_namespace.h.reason: Namespace-specific link handling is outside the first `ip link add nlmon0 type nlmon` MVP.

net/rtnetlink.h.reason: Expose `rtnl_link_ops`, `rtnl_link_register`, `rtnl_link_unregister`, and `netlink_ext_ack` for the link-type abstraction plan.

netlink_tap.reason: nlmon open/close lifecycle is defined around netlink tap registration.
required_surface: A private-state-owned tap handle that stores `dev` and `module` before registration.
Open/stop helper methods that call add/remove in matched lifecycle points.

translation.goal: Constrain the first `drivers/net/nlmon_rust.rs` to a minimal, artifact-driven smoke loop covering registration, setup, validate, open, stop, and xmit.
translation.abstraction_goal: Constrain Phase 4 so the first Rust loop reaches the `ip link add/up/down/del nlmon0` smoke closure without unconstrained driver invention.

mvp_scope.target_command: ip link add nlmon0 type nlmon && ip link set nlmon0 up && ip link show nlmon0 && ip link set nlmon0 down && ip link del nlmon0
mvp_scope.note: The first Rust loop must already cover the smoke-path lifecycle. `xmit` is required for `ip link set ... up`; `get_stats64` and `ethtool` parity can still land later.

body_plan: Only use the typed `netdevice::Device` setters listed in `setup_translation`.
Do not assign `netdev_ops` directly; the rtnl abstraction does that automatically.
Express the current MVP rule through `ValidateContext` only.
Access private state through the typed `private` argument only.
Access private state through the typed `private` argument only.
Receive the packet as owned `skbuff::SkBuff` and the device as shared `&netdevice::Device` only.
Return `netdevice::TxOutcome::Ok`; let the skb ownership discharge through the abstraction rather than explicit free calls in driver code.

type.note: Keep device type selection inside the typed `netdevice::Device` wrapper.

priv_flags.note: Preserve the `IFF_NO_QUEUE` setup bit without raw field access.

lltx.note: Keep lockless TX configuration in the wrapper layer.

netdev_ops.note: Do not assign `dev->netdev_ops` in driver code; the rtnl abstraction wires it before `setup`.

ethtool_ops.note: Keep `ethtool_ops` out of the first loop together with `always_on`.

needs_free_netdev.note: Keep free-on-destroy policy inside the wrapper.

features.note: Keep the feature bit expression inside the typed netdevice abstraction surface.

flags.note: Preserve the `IFF_NOARP` setup bit through the typed wrapper.

pcpu_stat_type.note: Keep the setup write for parity, but do not enable `ndo_get_stats64` yet.

mtu.note: Keep the softlimit MTU assignment explicit in `setup`, but hide bindgen-dependent constants behind the abstraction.

min_mtu.note: Expose the `nlmsghdr` size through the abstraction rather than direct bindgen usage in driver code.

init_policy.rust_requirement: The private type must accept the all-zero bit pattern (`Zeroable`).

fields.name: tap
fields.note: Own the netlink tap in Rust private storage; the MVP flow only uses it in open/stop.

actions.message: Oracle failure shows that the xmit path is part of the lifecycle-critical MVP surface for this scenario.
Oracle-driven correction: the first Rust loop must keep `start_xmit` ownership-safe and driver-side zero-unsafe.
